counterfactual_missing_items: Typical pyoderma gangrenosum ulceration with undermined borders
Erythema nodosum typically spares the face and lacks neutrophilic dermal infiltrate
IBD is a comorbid association, not the primary dermatologic diagnosis
decisive_items: new-onset flulike symptoms followed by low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques
Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration and intracorneal neutrophils
6 × 7-cm well-demarcated vegetative crusted plaques on the bilateral cheeks
response.rationale: R1 (Sweet syndrome) uniquely integrates the febrile prodrome, facial crusted plaques, and intradermal neutrophilic infiltrate with ulceration, matching the classic triad. R3 (IBD) explains the diarrhea and colonoscopy findings but is a secondary association; the skin and histopathology are not explained by IBD alone. R2 (pyoderma gangrenosum) is contradicted by the absence of typical ulcerative lesions and the presence of Miescher granulomas (more consistent with erythema nodosum). R4 (erythema nodosum) only captures the subcutaneous nodules and ignores the facial neutrophilic dermatosis and systemic features.

rejected.why: Miescher radial granulomas are characteristic of erythema nodosum, not pyoderma gangrenosum; no typical PG ulceration or undermined borders are described.
Only painful subcutaneous nodules are supportive; facial crusted plaques, neutrophilic infiltrate, and fever are unexplained, and EN does not present with facial vegetative plaques.
